To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a combined abnormality in HRV and QTc is strongly associated with cardiovascular death in type‐1 diabetic patients.
a combined abnormality in QTc interval and heart rate variability is a strong predictor for cardiovascular mortality in type 2 diabetes.
combined abnormality of heart rate variability and corrected QT interval is a strong independent predictor of mortality in patients with type 1 diabetes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of cardiovascular risk factors in type 1 diabetic individuals.
the identification and treatment of risk factors for premature death in type 2 diabetes.
the study of the relationship between heart rate variability and cardiovascular mortality in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the combination of abnormality in heart‐rate variability and QTc interval is a strong and independent predictor of cardiovascular mortality in type 2 diabetes, which is not explained by conventional risk factors.
the presence of a combined abnormality in HRV and QTc interval is associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular death in patients with type 1 diabetes.
a combined abnormality in HRV and QTc is associated with increased risk of cardiovascular mortality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
combined abnormality of heart rate variation and the corrected QT interval are strong predictors of mortality in type I diabetes independently of conventional cardiovascular risk factors.
a combined abnormality in both HRV and QTc is an independent predictor of mortality, and this is particularly so for cardiovascular death.
combined abnormality of heart rate variation and the QT corrected interval predicts premature death, and this effect is independent of conventional cardiovascular risk factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combined analysis of heart rate variability and the QTc interval is a strong and independent predictor of cardiovascular mortality in type 2 diabetes.
the combined abnormality in HRV and QTc is an independent and strong predictor of mortality.

combined abnormality of heart rate variation and the QT corrected interval is an important predictor of mortality from cardiovascular disease in type I diabetes, and that this risk factor should be taken into consideration when planning future screening and treatment programs.
